title: First 30 Days After a Death
description: A step-by-step list of what families commonly handle in the first month after a loved one dies.
intro: The weeks after a death are hard, and the paperwork can feel endless. Not everything is urgent. This list groups tasks by timing so you can focus on what matters first.

sections.heading: First 24 to 48 hours
items: Get a legal pronouncement of death from a doctor, hospice, or hospital
Contact the funeral home or cremation provider
Notify close family and friends
Arrange care for any dependents and pets
Secure the home, vehicles, and valuables
Look for funeral wishes and any prepaid funeral contract

sections.heading: First week
items: Order multiple certified copies of the death certificate
Find the original will, trust, and other planning documents
Make funeral or memorial arrangements
Write and publish an obituary
Notify the person's employer and ask about final pay and benefits
Forward the mail to a trusted person's address

sections.heading: Weeks two and three
items: Contact an estate planning or probate attorney
Notify Social Security and the post office
Notify banks, brokerage firms, and retirement plan administrators
Contact life insurance companies to start claims
Notify credit card companies and the three credit bureaus
Contact the Department of Veterans Affairs if the person served

sections.heading: Weeks three and four
items: Make a list of assets and debts
Open probate if needed, or begin trust administration
Open an estate bank account once the executor has authority
Keep paying essential bills, such as mortgage, utilities, and insurance
Cancel subscriptions, memberships, and the driver's license
Keep a log of every call, payment, and decision

sections.heading: Things to avoid
items: Avoid paying the deceased person's debts from your own money
Avoid selling or giving away property before the executor has authority
Avoid closing accounts that may be needed for estate payments
Avoid making large decisions without asking the executor or attorney
